The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. It removes scripts and event handlers everywhere, except inside Applications are exposed when an attacker can influence the SVG of the icons they render. The sources are the same as for CVE-2026-55877, like local icon files and the responses of the Iconify API.

The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. When the sanitizer changes an icon, it writes the icon out again as HTML. HTML writes the content of some elements, like <style>, without escaping it. But inside an <svg>, browsers parse the content of a <style> element as markup. Escaped markup in such an element then becomes live in the page:

<path onclick="x"/><style xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"><img src=x onerror=alert(1)></style>

The event handler of the <path> element only makes the sanitizer change the icon. Depending on the version, this affects every <style> element, or the elements of the XHTML namespace, like <style>, <xmp> or <noembed>.

On 2.x, the elements of the XHTML namespace were also kept. An XHTML <form> or <base> element then becomes live where icons are parsed as XML, like in the Google Maps bridge of ux-map.

Applications are exposed when an attacker can influence the SVG of the icons they render. The sources are the same as for CVE-2026-55877, like local icon files and the responses of the Iconify API.

On 2.x, the sanitizer now writes icons out as XML, which escapes their text, and only keeps the elements of the SVG namespace. On 3.x, it now only keeps the elements of the SVG namespace.

The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. Browsers parse an inline

, or . They then parse the rest of the icon as HTML, and they also parse the content of and <desc> elements as HTML. The sanitizer only checked icons as SVG, so an icon could contain markup that becomes live once parsed as HTML. For example, after a <p> element, a comment can end a <style> element early and add an <img> element with an event handler: <p/><style><!--</style><img src=1 onerror=alert(1)>--></style> In the same way, an icon could add a <base> element to the page, which changes where its relative links and forms go. It could also add a <meta> element that redirects the page. Comments were kept too, while browsers end a comment at <!--> or <!--->. The rest of such a comment then became live markup, even without any HTML element before it. Applications are exposed when an attacker can influence the SVG of the icons they render. The sources are the same as for CVE-2026-55877, like local icon files and the responses of the Iconify API. The sanitizer now removes comments and the elements that make browsers switch to HTML, and only keeps the text of <title> and <desc> elements. It also makes sure that markup in CDATA sections and attribute values can't end a <noscript> element around the icon.

#[AsLiveComponent(route: '...')] makes a live component send its requests to another route. The documentation suggests it so that the component lives under a specific firewall, for example. The default /_components/{_live_component}/{_live_action} route still served the component, though. A request to it rendered the component and ran its actions outside the firewall and the access rules of the configured route.

The request needs props signed by the application, which a page that rendered the component provides. Controller attributes on the component, like #[IsGranted], still applied.

A live component is now only served by the route it is configured with.

The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. The checks matched attribute names as written in the icon, while browsers and the renderer read some names differently.

On 2.x, fromFile() keys the attributes of the root <svg> element by their local name. A handler like x:onload passed the check, and was then rendered as onload, which runs on load. HTML parsers also read attribute names case-insensitively, so a SMIL animation with ATTRIBUTENAME="href" could set a javascript: URL on a link. And an href in the XLink namespace under another prefix, like q:href, wasn't checked. On 3.x, the sanitizer writes it out as xlink:href, and XML parsers resolve the prefix on both branches.

Applications are exposed when an attacker can influence the SVG of the icons they render. The sources are the same as for CVE-2026-55877, like local icon files and the responses of the Iconify API.

The sanitizer now checks attributes by local name. It also finds the attributeName of animations in any case, and ignores the prefix of its value.

The @symfony/stimulus-bridge npm package includes a Webpack loader called lazy-controller-loader that supports "magic comments" placed above a Stimulus controller import, for example /* stimulusFetch: 'lazy' */, to control lazy loading behavior. To read those options, the loader extracted the raw text of any stimulus* comment and evaluated it as JavaScript using Node's vm.runInNewContext(). The Node.js node:vm module is not a security sandbox, and a crafted comment can break out of the VM context using well-known techniques to run arbitrary Node.js code within the build process.

This is a build-time vulnerability: it does not affect browsers or end users. The code executes on the developer machine or CI/build server during a Webpack or Symfony Encore build. Realistic attack vectors include a malicious Stimulus controller introduced through a compromised dependency, or a pull request that triggers an automated CI build. An attacker who can get such a file into the build can read files and environment variables available to the build process, exfiltrate CI secrets, tamper with generated build artifacts, and run commands with the permissions of the build user.

The loader no longer evaluates comment content as JavaScript. It now parses each comment as an object expression using a real JavaScript parser and extracts only plain literal values. Any non-literal value, such as a function call, an identifier, or a sequence expression, is rejected and reported as a build error instead of being executed. Legitimate option values like 'lazy' and 'eager' continue to work without any changes required on the user's side.

The controllers.json loader of @symfony/stimulus-bridge loads the package.json file of each package listed in controllers.json with require(). Node resolves this path through the exports field of the package, which can map ./package.json to a script. require() then runs that script during the Webpack or Symfony Encore build.

This is a build-time vulnerability: it doesn't affect browsers or end users. A malicious or compromised package listed in controllers.json can run code on the developer machine or the CI server. This works even when the package manager doesn't run install scripts. This code can read the files and environment variables of the build, like CI secrets, and change the built assets.

The loader now reads the resolved file and parses it as JSON, so that a mapped script fails to parse instead of running.

A path traversal vulnerability in the File Explorer share-link upload component allows a remote attacker with a folder-scoped upload share link to upload or overwrite files in the shared folder's immediate parent directory due to missing trailing validation prior to path canonicalization.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A path traversal vulnerability in the File Explorer share-link folder-listing endpoint allows a remote attacker with a folder-scoped share link to list directory contents outside the shared folder, including other Samba shares readable by the link creator, because path validation occurs before path canonicalization.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

Since the fix for CVE-2025-64500, Request::getPathInfo() strips the script name from the start of the URL. It does so even when the script name is only the start of a longer path segment. With SCRIPT_NAME set to /index.php, a request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /admin and is routed like /admin. Encoded spellings such as /index%2Ephpadmin or /%69ndex.phpadmin work too. Before that fix, the path info was admin, which no route matched.

Rules enforced by Symfony are not affected: access_control and firewalls read the same path info as the router. Rules enforced in front of PHP are. The nginx configuration of the Symfony documentation and the .htaccess file of symfony/apache-pack make /index.php/admin unreachable, but they pass /index.phpadmin to the front controller. So a location /admin block in nginx, a <Location /admin> section in Apache, or a CDN or WAF rule on /admin can be bypassed.

The script name is now stripped only when it is followed by /, ? or the end of the URL. A request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /index.phpadmin.

When Request::getBaseUrl() does not find the script name at the start of the request URI, it looks for it further into the path. This supports web servers that rewrite every URL to a front controller in a subdirectory. The base URL then kept everything before the script name, and the client chooses that part. A request URI starting with // or /\ made the base URL start with a host.

With SCRIPT_NAME=/public/index.php, a request for //evil.example/public/index.php/login is routed to /login, with the base URL //evil.example/public/index.php and the base path //evil.example/public. The URLs generated for that page then point to evil.example:
- links built with path() and the actions of forms, so a login form sends the credentials of the user to evil.example;
- redirects to generated URLs, such as the ones of redirectToRoute();
- assets referenced with a relative path through asset(), so the page can load scripts from evil.example.

The attacker has to make a user follow a crafted link, such as https://app.example//evil.example/public/index.php/login. framework.trusted_hosts does not help, since the host of the request is the real one.

Applications are affected when their front controller is in a subdirectory and the web server sends it URIs that do not start with that directory. A .htaccess file at the root of the project that rewrites every URL to public/ does that, for instance.

Applications are also affected when the web server sets SCRIPT_NAME to the path of the request. Some nginx configurations do that when they send every request to the front controller without fastcgi_split_path_info. php -S does it too, with a router script outside the document root. A request for /\evil.example/index.php then gets the base URL /\evil.example/index.php, which browsers read as a link to evil.example.

The configurations recommended in the Symfony documentation are not affected.

Request::getBaseUrl() now returns an empty base URL when the request URI starts with // or /\.

Most methods of Symfony\Component\Filesystem\Path rely on Path::split(), which takes everything before the first :// as the root of a path. It doesn't check that this prefix is a URI scheme, so the .. segments in that prefix are never resolved. PHP sees a scheme only at the start of a string. So /base/../x://../secret.txt is a plain local path to /secret.txt for PHP, while Path::isBasePath('/base', '/base/../x://../secret.txt') returns true. canonicalize(), join(), makeAbsolute() and makeRelative() are affected the same way.

Some applications check a path built from user input with isBasePath() or canonicalize(), and then open it. They can be made to read or write files outside the expected directory.

On Symfony 6.4 and later, the AssetMapper component builds with Path::join() the path of the files that a remote package references from its CSS. A malicious or compromised package can therefore make importmap:require or importmap:install write a file of its choice outside assets/vendor. For example, the CSS url(../../../../../public/x://shell.php) writes public/x:/shell.php.

A prefix is now a scheme only when PHP would look for a stream wrapper with that name. That is two or more letters, digits, +, - or ., followed by :// at the start of the path. Other prefixes are regular path segments, and the .. segments after them are resolved. Real schemes such as phar://, file://, vfs:// or compress.zlib:// keep working.

The fix for CVE-2026-45756 lowers pcre.backtrack_limit to 10000 around each preg_match() call of the match() and search() filter functions. That limit applies to one starting position, not to one call. PCRE resets its counter at every position it tries a match from. So an unanchored pattern that stays just under the limit is paid once per byte of the subject. Each call also starts from a fresh limit, so chaining clauses in one filter multiplies the work.

Two other paths made the cost of a query grow faster than its size, without any regular expression:
- The filter evaluator scanned the whole expression for logical operators once per node. Its cost grew with the square of the number of chained clauses.
- Queries starting with $ inside a filter, like @.x == $.limit or length($.items), were evaluated again for every node the filter visits.

An application that evaluates an attacker-influenced JSONPath expression can therefore still be made to hold a PHP worker. A document of 2 MB and a query of 2.5 KB take 3.5 minutes of CPU.

JsonCrawler::find() now bounds the total regex work of one call, and throws an exception when that budget is exhausted. Filter expressions are parsed once per query, and absolute queries inside filters are evaluated once per query.

Missing authentication in the conversation session resource handling of Unblu inc. Unblu Spark 7.0 through 7.57.10 and 8.0 before 8.38.0, on on-premises and cloud deployments, allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to download a resource of a conversation session via its exact URL, without an agent session.



The resource URLs contain random identifiers that can't be guessed, so the attacker must obtain the exact URL of a resource first.
A logical flaw vulnerability exists in the ZTE Nubia RedMagic 9S Pro+. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may compromise confidentiality.

Z80 Ultra is affected by an information disclosure vulnerability in service interfaces related to application scenarios. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may result in an impact on confidentiality.
Z80 Ultra product has an improper access control vulnerability in the game assistant module. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may affect confidentiality and integrity.
Z80 Ultra product has an improper modification control vulnerability. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may affect integrity and availability.

A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the initialization component of ADM. When the NAS is uninitialized, the endpoint accepts an unauthenticated sid query parameter and inserts its URL-decoded value into an inline JavaScript string without proper JavaScript-context encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker can craft a malicious URL that, when opened by a user, executes arbitrary JavaScript in the ADM management origin. Successful exploitation may allow manipulation of the setup page and execution of same-origin requests in the victim's browser. The vulnerability is limited to the first-run initialization state.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

Insufficient bounds checks in the Link Aggregation handler of ASUSTOR ADM allow an authenticated administrator to submit an excessive number of interface tokens. Crafted requests can corrupt memory and terminate the affected privileged CGI process.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Wi-Fi connection handler of ADM allows an authenticated administrator to corrupt heap memory and terminate the affected CGI request by supplying an oversized Wi-Fi pre-shared key.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An improper authorization vulnerability exists in the wallpaper component of ADM. An authenticated, low-privileged user can bypass shared-folder access controls by specifying an image path within a restricted share. The CGI processes the request with root privileges without enforcing the source share's access permissions, allowing the attacker to copy and retrieve images they are not authorized to access, resulting in unauthorized information disclosure.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

Authorization bypass using a user-controlled token (IDOR) on the GlobalEduca job portal. The GET endpoint ‘/attachments/{attachment_id}’ fails to verify whether the attachment belongs to the authenticated user. A user with a registered account can enumerate sequential identifiers and download attachments belonging to other candidates, including resumes containing personal data.

An SQL injection vulnerability exists in the firewall management component of ADM Defender due to insufficient validation and improper handling of input data in SQLite queries. This vulnerability may allow an attacker with access to the affected functionality to manipulate database queries, potentially resulting in unauthorized access to or modification of firewall-related data.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

In Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK versions 2.0.0-milestone-10 to 2.0.0-milestone-16, the destination validation of the Operation Delegation feature, introduced to prevent server-side request forgery (CVE-2026-7412), can be bypassed through DNS rebinding.



Before dispatching a delegated Operation invocation, the server resolves the host of the `invocationDelegation` qualifier URI and rejects loopback, private, link-local, multicast and cloud metadata addresses. The outbound HTTP client (Reactor Netty), however, performs its own, independent DNS lookup when opening the connection and does not use the validated addresses. An attacker who can create or update a Submodel Operation and controls the DNS records of the delegation host can answer the validation lookup with a public address and the connection lookup with an internal address. No authentication is required when the authorization feature is not enabled.



Invoking the Operation then causes the BaSyx server to send HTTP POST requests to destinations the protection is meant to block, such as services in internal IT/OT networks, loopback-only interfaces, or cloud metadata endpoints. The server can be used to pivot into network segments that are not directly reachable by the attacker.



Only deployments with the Operation Delegation feature enabled are affected. The feature is enabled by default.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK 2.0.0-milestone-17.

Cross-site scripting in the conversation file-sharing feature of Unblu inc. Unblu Spark 7.0 through 7.57.10 and 8.0 before 8.41.1, on on-premises and cloud deployments, allows an unauthenticated remote attacker in the visitor role to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of a user who opens a crafted link to a file the attacker uploaded, via a file type that the browser renders as active content, such as SVG.



The JavaScript runs in the context and under the identity of that user's session.



Exploitation requires the victim to open the crafted link.

Missing Authentication for Critical Function in Apache Texera (incubating).



The Python virtual environment (PVE) management endpoints of a computing unit are not authenticated by the application itself. In the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments, which place no authenticating gateway in front of the services, these endpoints are reachable without credentials. The Kubernetes deployment gates them at the gateway, so only the Kubernetes deployment provides the full security model described in SECURITY.md.



This issue affects Apache Texera (incubating): from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0.



Users are recommended to use the Kubernetes deployment, which enforces the full security model, and to upgrade to 1.3.0-incubating, which documents that the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in 'carta_presentacion[contenido]' field in the POST request to '/personas/{persona_id}/cvs/{cv_id}/carta_presentaciones' on the job portal. The server stores the data entered by an authenticated candidate and displays it in the recruitment interface without sanitizing it. When reviewing an application, the recruiter’s browser can execute the injected JavaScript code within the context of their session on the portal.

Uploading PDF files with active content to the languages form. The POST endpoint ‘/people/{person_id}/languages’ checks the declared MIME type and allows an authenticated user to upload a PDF with embedded JavaScript. The portal serves the file via a GET request to ‘/attachments/{attachment_id}’ with the ‘Content-Disposition: inline’ header, so it can be opened in the browser’s PDF viewer during review. The handling of active content depends on the viewer used.

Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in 'experiencia_laboral[descripcion]' field in the POST request to '/personas/{persona_id}/experiencias_laborales' on the job portal. The server stores the data entered by an authenticated candidate and displays it in the recruitment interface without sanitizing it. When reviewing an application, the recruiter’s browser can execute the injected JavaScript code within the context of their session on the portal.

Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in 'activity[description]' field in the POST request to '/people/{person_id}/cvs/{cv_id}/activities' on the job portal. The server stores the data entered by an authenticated candidate and displays it in the recruitment interface without sanitizing it. When reviewing an application, the recruiter’s browser can execute the injected JavaScript code within the context of their session on the portal.

The SUSE NeuVector image scanner before version 4.331 writes each per-scan task request to a temporary file on disk with mode 0644 (world-readable). This could allow local attackers to gain the registry access credentials of the scanned images.

TypesenseVectorStore is vulnerable to a document ID injection in its delete operation that can cause unintended documents to be deleted.



 TypesenseVectorStore.doDelete(List<String>) builds a Typesense filter_by expression by raw string concatenation of caller-supplied document IDs into the form id: [id1,id2,...] . The Typesense id field uses bare (unquoted) values in this list form with no escaping mechanism. An ID containing characters with syntactic meaning in the Typesense filter grammar — such as a comma ( , ), a closing bracket ( ] ), or operator tokens ( || , && ) — can break out of the list literal and alter the structure of the filter expression.



 An attacker who controls a document ID passed to the delete operation can use this to delete documents other than the intended ones (comma injection), or to construct a filter that matches every document in the collection (operator breakout), resulting in unintended bulk deletion.



 Applications that pass externally supplied or user-controlled document IDs to VectorStore.delete(List<String>) backed by TypesenseVectorStore are affected.

Description

`HostURLFilter.configure` reads the `ignoreOutsideDomain` parameter but tests the node belonging to
`ignoreOutsideHost` when deciding whether the domain mode was configured. A filter configuration that
names only `ignoreOutsideDomain`, which the class documentation presents as an independent mode, is
therefore discarded: the flag is forced to false, `filter` short-circuits on its guard and every URL is
returned unchanged. The filter enforces nothing while appearing to be configured, and the failure is
silent. The mirror-image configuration, naming only `ignoreOutsideHost`, fails with a
`NullPointerException` while the topology is starting.

The effect is the loss of a scope control the operator configured, so a crawled page's outlinks are
followed to hosts the operator intended to exclude. Impact beyond crawl scope depends on what the
crawler then fetches and is not claimed here. Projects generated from the StormCrawler Maven archetypes
are not affected, because all three shipped filter configurations set both parameters.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 4.0.0, where each parameter is tested independently. Operators whose configuration sets only
`ignoreOutsideDomain` will find the crawl restricted to the source domain, as configured, which may
reduce the number of outlinks accepted.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should set both `ignoreOutsideHost` and `ignoreOutsideDomain`
explicitly in the `HostURLFilter` configuration, which produces the intended behaviour on affected
versions.

Credit

Independently reported to the Apache StormCrawler PMC by n0mi1k, with a proof of concept.

Also found by the ASF -- using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated
and reported by Apache StormCrawler.

Description

`CookieConverter.getCookies` decides which stored cookies to attach to an outbound request. The
applicability check is nested inside a test for the presence of a `Domain` attribute, so a cookie
without one, which is the ordinary form of a session cookie, skips scoping entirely and is returned for
whatever target URL was passed. RFC 6265 requires the opposite: a cookie with no `Domain` attribute is
host-only and belongs to the host that set it.

Two further defects sit in the same method. The domain comparison has no notion of a registrable
domain, so a `Domain` value of `com` matches every host under it, and the comparison returns true when
it throws, so a failure to evaluate the check admits the cookie. Neither the converter nor
`MetadataTransfer`, which carries the stored cookie to outlinks, ever considers the host that issued
it.

Cookie handling is opt-in: it requires `http.use.cookies` to be set to true, which is not the default,
and the cookie key to be listed in `metadata.transfer`. The documented recipe does not work as written,
because the `metadata.transfer` example in the internals documentation names `set-cookie` while the key
present in metadata is `protocol.set-cookie` and the transfer matches key names exactly. Deployments
affected are therefore those where an operator determined the correct key, enabled cookie handling and
crawls an authenticated site whose pages link or redirect to other hosts. In that case the session
cookie of the authenticated origin is sent to those hosts.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 4.0.0, where a cookie without a `Domain` attribute is sent only to the host that set it, a
single-label domain is rejected and the domain check fails closed. Because the protocol does not yet
record the host that issued a cookie, cookies without a `Domain` attribute are not sent at all until
that host is recorded; operators relying on cookie transfer will notice this. The documentation error
is corrected in the same release.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should confine an authenticated crawl to a topology whose URL
filters keep it on the origin that issued the credentials, and should not rely on cookie scoping as a
boundary. Rotating session credentials used for such crawls is advisable.

Credit

Independently reported to the Apache StormCrawler PMC by n0mi1k, with a proof of concept.

Also found by the ASF -- using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated
and reported by Apache StormCrawler.

Description

The SQL status backend serialises per-URL metadata into a single column by concatenating a tabulation,
the key, an equals sign and the value, with no escaping. On read-back the string is split on the same
two characters, so the round trip is not injective: a value that contains a tabulation returns as one
or more additional keys that were never written.

Values on that path are supplied by crawled servers. `FetcherBolt` records the raw `Location` header of
a redirect as `_redirTo`, and `_redirTo` is part of the default `metadata.persist` set, so a redirect
whose `Location` contains a tabulation followed by `key=value` pairs introduces those keys into the
crawler's own control metadata on the next scheduling cycle. Several control keys are read without a
prefix, so the injected keys are live: `http.proxy.host`, `http.proxy.port`, `http.proxy.user` and
`http.proxy.pass` among them, as well as scheduling and request-shaping keys such as `depth`,
`max.depth`, `crawl.delay`, `http.content.limit` and `isSitemap`.

Where a proxy manager is configured, the consequence is not limited to corrupted scheduling data.
`SingleProxyManager.getProxy(Metadata)` consults the per-URL metadata first and returns what it finds,
so an injected proxy host and port take precedence over the operator's configured proxy and subsequent
fetches, together with any configured `Authorization` header, are routed through a host the crawled
content chose. A related defect in `AbstractStatusUpdaterBolt` compounds this: an injected
`status.store.as.is.with.nextfetchdate` that is not a valid instant escapes the enclosing try/catch and
stops the bolt, and because the stored row is replayed the failure repeats.

Deployments using the OpenSearch or Solr status backends are unaffected, because those serialise
metadata structurally.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 4.0.0, where the metadata column is written in an escaped form behind a format marker, rows
written by earlier versions are still decoded unchanged, and the stored next-fetch-date is parsed
defensively.

The fix does not repair rows written before the upgrade. Operators using the SQL status backend should
inspect the metadata column of an existing status table for tabulation characters and remove the
affected rows, and should assume any proxy credentials configured for the crawl may have been exercised
through an attacker-chosen proxy and rotate them. Users who cannot upgrade immediately can remove
`_redirTo` from `metadata.persist` to close the demonstrated path, though other crawled values reaching
persisted metadata remain.

Credit

Independently reported to the Apache StormCrawler PMC by n0mi1k, with a proof of concept.

Also found by the ASF -- using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated
and reported by Apache StormCrawler.

Description

When StormCrawler fetches a host's `/robots.txt` and receives a redirect, `HttpRobotRulesParser`
resolves the `Location` header and re-fetches the target for up to five hops. The loop checks neither
the scheme, the host nor the port of the resolved target, and it is not governed by
`http.allow.redirects`, which only affects the page fetch. A crawled site can therefore point the
robots.txt fetch at any address reachable from the fetcher worker, including loopback interfaces,
private ranges and cloud metadata endpoints. Every crawled URL triggers a robots.txt fetch on a cache
miss, so no unusual configuration is required to reach the loop.

The fetched body is only parsed as robots rules and is not returned to the caller, so the read itself
is blind. The more direct impact is on credentials: the okhttp protocol applies its configured request
headers, including the `Authorization` header built from `http.basicauth.user` and
`http.basicauth.password` and anything in `http.custom.headers`, to every request it makes. Because
StormCrawler follows the redirect itself and issues a new request, okhttp's own removal of the
`Authorization` header across a host change does not apply, and the operator's crawl credentials are
delivered to the host the redirect names.

The connection-time IP filter, `http.filter.ipaddress.include` and `http.filter.ipaddress.exclude`, is
installed as an okhttp network interceptor on the same client and does apply to these hops when it is
configured. It ships with no rules, which is why the path is reachable in a default configuration. URL
filtering never applies, because the robots.txt fetch does not pass through the outlink filter chain.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 4.0.0, where a robots.txt redirect is followed only when the target uses http or https and
shares scheme, host and port with the URL it was reached from. Deployments that legitimately serve
robots.txt through a cross-host redirect can restore the previous behaviour with
`http.robots.redirect.crosshost.allow`.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should set `http.filter.ipaddress.exclude` to cover loopback,
private, link-local and CGNAT ranges, which is enforced after DNS resolution and therefore also on
redirect hops. Operators who configure `http.basicauth.*` or `http.custom.headers` for a crawl should
assume those credentials may have been sent to third-party hosts and rotate them, and should scope
credentials by running a separate topology per origin.

An API which can allow a user to delete any workflow execution results is missing authentication. This means that any workflow result could be deleted by someone able to reach the Texera instance.



This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in the computing unit workflow websocket of Apache Texera (incubating) allows an authenticated user to view workflow results, control workflow executions, and run code in a computing unit they have not been granted. In local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments this is possible directly; in Kubernetes deployments it is possible from code running inside another computing unit in the cluster.



This issue affects Apache Texera : from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0, which fixes the issue. Local JVM and Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in the project REST API of Apache Texera (incubating).



The project API did not check that the caller owns, or has been granted access to, the project being accessed. Any authenticated user with an approved account (the REGULAR or ADMIN role; new accounts need administrator approval by default) could view, modify or delete other users' projects, change which workflows those projects contain, and see the e-mail addresses of a project's owner and collaborators. The project feature is hidden in the web UI by default, but the API was reachable regardless of that setting.



This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue by removing the deprecated project feature and its data.



If you cannot upgrade immediately, configure the reverse proxy in front of Texera to reject every request whose path starts with /api/project, /api/public/project or /api/access/project, and every request whose path contains ';', which the Texera server ignores when routing. Respond with 403 or 404, not 401: from 1.2.0-incubating the web UI treats a 401 as an expired session, and the workflow pages request the project list when they load. Unless an administrator has enabled the project feature, this does not affect other functionality; those project-list requests are simply rejected. Make sure the Texera server is reachable only through that proxy.



Blocking and upgrading do not undo access obtained earlier. Before upgrading, review the project, project_user_access and workflow_of_project tables, which remain empty unless someone has used the feature, and remove rows you do not expect; the upgrade deletes these tables. Do not copy project grants into workflow_user_access without checking each one.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in the public project REST API of Apache Texera (incubating).



The public project API did not check that a project had been made public before granting the caller read access to it. Any authenticated user with an approved account (the REGULAR or ADMIN role; new accounts need administrator approval by default) could give themselves lasting read access to other users' private projects and to the private workflows in them, including their version and execution history. Only deployments in which users have created projects are affected; the project feature is hidden in the web UI by default.



This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue by removing the deprecated project feature and its data.

Unless an administrator has enabled the project feature, this does not affect other functionality; those project-list requests are simply rejected. Make sure the Texera server is reachable only through that proxy.



Blocking and upgrading do not undo access obtained earlier. Before upgrading, review the project_user_access table, which remains empty unless someone has used the feature: treat any READ grant on a project that is not listed in public_project, and that the project's owner did not give, as suspect. The upgrade deletes this table. Removing a grant does not remove copies the user may already have made of the workflows.

Reflected cross-site scripting in the versioned REST API documentation page in Checkmk versions 2.5.0 before 2.5.0p21 allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of a user who opens a crafted link, in the context of that user's Checkmk session. The API version segment of the documentation URL is inserted into the page without escaping, and the page is reachable without authentication.

Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Apache Allura's ticket tracking tool.



This issue affects Apache Allura: before 1.23.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.23.0, which fixes the issue.

XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls an object version id passed to ExAws.S3.delete_multiple_objects/3 to add objects to the batch delete.

delete_multiple_objects/3 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex builds the <Delete> request body by placing each object's version between <VersionId> tags without XML escaping. A version such as v1</VersionId></Object><Object><Key>important-file</Key></Object><Object><Key>x</Key><VersionId>v2 closes the caller's object and opens new ones, so S3 deletes objects the application never listed, including other users' objects in the same bucket.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 are vulnerable to an uncontrolled resource consumption issue in Rex::Proto::Http::Request#normalize!. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can send an HTTP request with a deeply nested path that triggers repeated rescans of the request target, causing quadratic CPU consumption and temporarily degrading the availability of any affected HTTP listener.

The issue is fixed in Metasploit Framework 6.5.10

XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls tag keys or values to inject forged tag entries into S3 object and bucket tagging requests.

ExAws.S3.put_object_tagging/4 and ExAws.S3.put_bucket_tagging/2 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex build the <TagSet> request body by interpolating tag keys and values directly into <Key> and <Value> elements via to_string/1, without applying the module's existing escape_xml_string/1 helper (which delete_multiple_objects already uses for object keys). An application that forwards user-supplied data as a tag key or value lets an attacker close the intended element and inject attacker-chosen <Tag> entries. For example, a tag value of blue</Value></Tag><Tag><Key>owner</Key><Value>admin turns one intended tag into two tags on the wire. Because S3 honors tags in access-control conditions (aws:RequestTag, s3:ExistingObjectTag) and cost-allocation reporting, an injected tag can forge an authorization-relevant tag or corrupt the intended tag set.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.2 before 2.6.0.

XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 (ExAws.S3 module) allows an attacker to inject arbitrary XML configuration elements into S3 bucket-configuration request bodies via unescaped, caller-supplied values.

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/s3.ex and program routines ExAws.S3.put_bucket_logging/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_notification/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_replication/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_website/2.

The bucket-configuration body builders construct their XML by interpolating caller-supplied values directly into the request body without escaping, and never route them through the module's own escape_xml_string/1 helper. A value containing XML metacharacters (<, >, &, quotes) can close the intended element early and open attacker-chosen elements, which the builder's trailing closing tag then closes, keeping the document single-rooted and well-formed. In a multi-tenant application where tenants configure their own bucket settings, an attacker who can influence one of the interpolated field values (for example the logging target, a notification ARN, a replication destination or Account, or a website redirect HostName) can inject arbitrary configuration nodes into a request the application signs and sends to AWS. The affected builders are reached through the public functions put_bucket_logging/2, put_bucket_notification/2, put_bucket_replication/2, and put_bucket_website/2.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.5.9 before 2.6.0.

brute-force protection.

SolarWinds Serv-U is affected by an out-of-bounds

A flaw was found in rsyslog. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can trigger a stack-based buffer overflow by sending a malformed log message containing an embedded IPv4-in-IPv6 address to an instance configured with the mmanon anonymization module. This flaw causes the logging service to crash, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

HortusFox is a self-hosted web application for collaborative plant management. Prior to 6.2, the toggle_boolean_value() handler in app/controller/admin.php passes the name parameter of the /admin/environment/boolean/toggle route in app/config/routes.php to AppModel::updateSingle() in app/models/AppModel.php, which concatenates the parameter into the SQL UPDATE identifier position without validation. An unauthenticated attacker can induce a signed-in administrator to open a crafted link, causing SQL injection that permits expressions and subqueries to read database contents, including an administrator password hash, or modify settings to enable passwordless administrator access. The hash alone does not permit direct login. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.

Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.0.0 until 3.1.13, peer certificates were parsed and their RSA public keys were passed to handshake signature and certificate-chain verification without an explicit modulus-size limit. A remote peer can provide a certificate with an unusually large attacker-chosen RSA modulus and an invalid signature; no corresponding private key or valid handshake signature is required to trigger the expensive operation. An RSA verification path must execute. A local ECDSA certificate does not prevent the peer from presenting an RSA certificate, and WebRTC deployments can be affected. Repeated or concurrent malicious handshakes can consume substantial CPU resources, delay legitimate connections, and reduce service availability. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.13.

Insert Pages plugin for WordPress (insert-pages) before 3.11.6 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the insert_pages_handle_shortcode_insert() function that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access or above to read draft, pending, scheduled, and private posts they do not own. Attackers can reference sequential post IDs in the [insert page] shortcode to render the full content, title, excerpt, and metadata of unpublished posts, since the function checks a generic read capability instead of enforcing the read_post meta capability tied to post author and status.

EpicStaff 1.2.0 before 1.3.1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in DocumentViewSet download and copy endpoints that allows authenticated users to access other organizations' documents. Attackers holding Knowledge Sources permissions in one organization can enumerate sequential document IDs to download or copy foreign documents, or insert documents into another organization's collection.

Mercur @mercurjs/core before 2.3.2 contains a missing object-level authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated vendors to access other sellers by substituting the :id path parameter. Attackers can read payment and tax details, overwrite profiles and addresses, and invite, remove, or re-role team members to take over another vendor's store.

Spug before 4.1.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrator users to read per-host SSH private keys through the GET /api/host/ endpoint. Users granted a host can read the cleartext pkey field returned by Host.to_view and log in directly over SSH, bypassing Spug's permissions and audit trail even after revocation.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in SDP_ParseAttribute that allows attackers to cause unbounded memory growth via a NUL byte in an a=fmtp line. Attackers can supply a crafted .sdp file or malicious RTSP DESCRIBE response to hang gf_sdp_info_parse and exhaust memory, causing denial of service.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the glTF 1.0 importer that allows attackers to read adjacent heap memory by supplying an unchecked KHR_binary_glTF image bufferView. Attackers can craft a glTF or GLB file whose bufferView byteOffset or byteLength exceeds its buffer, disclosing heap memory through embedded texture data or crashing the process.

Dell Virtual Storage Integrator for VMware vSphere Web Client, versions prior to 10.12.0.0, contains a Use of Hard-coded Credentials vulnerability in ssl_config.properties. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to credential exposure.

SolarWinds Serv-U is affected by denial-of-service 
vulnerability that may allow users with privileged access 
to cause too much memory usage, causing the server to 
reject new connections. A specific configuration is 
required, and an SMTP server must be set up.
Dell PowerStore contains a weak password-storage vulnerability that could allow an attacker with access to the credential store to recover user passwords by offline brute force.

Adobe Campaign Classic (ACC) is affected by an Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user. A low-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.

Adobe Campaign Classic (ACC) is affected by a reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to inject malicious scripts into a web page, potentially gaining elevated access or control over the victim's account or session. Exploitation of this issue requires user interaction in that a victim must visit a maliciously crafted URL or interact with a compromised web page. Scope is changed.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.67 to 0.11.2, organization and team billing-manager roles intended only for spend management are treated as ordinary members across workflow, run, library, and marketplace routes. Although the role matrix in autogpt_platform/autogpt_libs/autogpt_libs/auth/permissions.py withholds run access and workflow creation, those routes do not enforce the matrix and their underlying membership lookups ignore the caller's role. As a result, a team billing manager can read team workflows and other members' runs (including inputs, outputs, and per-node data), while an organization billing manager can view shared workflows and runs and create workflows and marketplace listings; neither can modify or delete other members' workflows. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.3.

Adobe Experience Manager is affected by a DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this issue by manipulating the DOM environment to execute malicious JavaScript within the context of the victim's browser. Exploitation of this issue requires user interaction in that a victim must visit a crafted webpage. Scope is changed.

Adobe Experience Manager is affected by an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine vulnerability that could result in a Security feature bypass. An attacker with high privileges could leverage this vulnerability to bypass security measures and gain unauthorized read and write access. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.

Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic in the query construction of AWS Graph Explorer before 3.2.1 might allow an authenticated remote user with write access to the connected graph database to access and modify data in that database with Graph Explorer's privileges via a crafted property key or label that is used when another user performs a search.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to Graph Explorer version 3.2.1 or later.

A stack-based buffer overflow in the replication origin name parsing component in AWS pgactive before 2.1.10 might allow an authenticated remote user to execute arbitrary operating system commands as the database operating system user via a crafted replication origin name.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to pgactive version 2.1.10 or later.

Improper removal of sensitive information in the troubleshooting tool in the Amazon ECS MCP Server (awslabs.ecs-mcp-server) before 0.1.36 might allow a remote actor who can influence the agent's input to obtain cleartext container environment variable values and secret references from ECS task definitions, which the server's sensitive data setting is intended to redact, via prompt injection that causes the agent to request troubleshooting guidance.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 0.1.36 or later and rotate any credentials stored as plaintext task definition environment variables.

A security flaw has been discovered in Volans NGFW Next-Generation Firewall r5.1. The affected element is an unknown function of the file include/sqlite3.inc of the component Web Management Interface. Performing a manipulation results in sql injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

ntop n2n supernode 3.0 through 3.1.1 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to leak memory and execute code by sending an untrusted 16-bit auth token_size in REGISTER_SUPER_NAK datagrams. Attackers can register an edge in a chosen community, then send an oversized token_size to leak stack canaries and pointers, overwrite the return address, or crash the supernode.

Canvas 7.0.0 before 7.2.11 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Contributors to inject scripts by exploiting a libxml2 parser differential in PostBody::clean(). Attackers can publish posts with slash-separated event handler attributes rendered unescaped in show.blade.php, hijacking Editor or Admin sessions to escalate their role to Admin.

Obtainium before 1.7.5 trusts the allowIdChange field in imported app data, allowing attackers to bypass the package ID mismatch check by delivering crafted obtainium://app deep links. Once a victim confirms the import, attackers can silently replace a tracked app with an attacker-controlled source and install a different APK, prompt-free when Shizuku or root is authorized.

AppStream 0.14.5 before 1.2.3 contains a division by zero vulnerability in asc_read_translation_status() in compose/asc-utils-l10n.c that allows attackers to crash compose runs via crafted Qt .qm files. Attackers can supply a valid .qm file with no TRANSLATION records, triggering SIGFPE that terminates the entire appstreamcli compose or libappstream-compose process.

DeepSpeed _get_zero_stage Deserialization of Untrusted Data Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of DeepSpeed. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of checkpoint data. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in deserialization of untrusted data. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-29242.

BusyBox ftpd Directory Traversal Arbitrary File Read and Write Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to create or delete arbitrary files or disclose sensitive information on affected installations of BusyBox. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the ftpd service, which listens on TCP port 21 by default. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied path prior to using it in file operations. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create or delete files or disclose information in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-27555.

Server-side request forgery in Amazon OpenSearch Service service software before R20260720 might allow an authenticated user with permission to manage snapshots to make the service send requests to network destinations of their choosing via the snapshot repository endpoint setting. This issue is addressed in service software R20260720. Customers should update their domains to R20260720 or later.

A flaw was found in the file-psd plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted PSD (Photoshop Document) image file in LAB color mode, the plugin does not properly validate that a fourth channel is present when the transparency flag is set. This mismatch causes the merged-image path to allocate buffers for three components while performing color conversion with four-component formats, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow. This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

browser-use before 1.0.0 contains a URL parser differential vulnerability in SecurityWatchdog that allows attackers to bypass allowed_domains, prohibited_domains, and block_ip_addresses checks by crafting a URL with a backslash before the allowed host, exploiting the mismatch between urllib.parse hostname extraction and Chromium's WHATWG-style URL parsing. Attackers can influence an LLM-controlled navigate action, such as through prompt injection, to send requests to loopback or private addresses or arbitrary external hosts before the browser redirects to about:blank, enabling SSRF and persistent state changes on the target server.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.1 through 0.10.0, credentials are sent to a third party when a redirect's Location header hides the new host behind a backslash. A signed-in user who connects an MCP server URL, or runs a shared or marketplace workflow with a host-scoped credential, can have that credential delivered to a third party if the host responds with a redirect whose Location the other party influenced. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.10.0, a user can add a version under another user's workflow ID and take over its Marketplace listing. An attacker with an account and the target's workflow ID can replace the creator's pending Marketplace submission with their own, so that approval installs the attacker's workflow under the creator's listing. Without reviewer involvement, the attacker can also stop the owner from saving new versions and break runs that name no version. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

A vulnerability was identified in GongShengyue OnlineBooks up to dfc5eacc08d3b0396c266049548618f6fb9587ea. This vulnerability affects the function insert of the file src/cn/ylcto/book/filter/AdminLoginFilter.java of the component BooksServlet. The manipulation leads to missing authorization. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. This product follows a rolling release approach for continuous delivery, so version details for affected or updated releases are not provided. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CubeWP Forms before 1.1.13 contains an unauthenticated stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious JavaScript by submitting unregistered field names through the public REST route cubewp-custom-form/v1/submit/, which bypasses its own nonce check and saves unsanitized values due to a missing default case in the sanitizer, later rendered unescaped on the admin Leads detail page. Attackers can send a single crafted GET request containing a script payload in a custom form field to execute arbitrary JavaScript in an administrator's wp-admin session when the lead is viewed, enabling full site takeover such as creating a new administrator account.

VeraCrypt before 1.26.30 on Linux contains a command injection vulnerability in CoreUnix::CheckFilesystem that allows a local attacker with same-UID access and an active elevated CoreService session to execute arbitrary commands by injecting an unsanitized VirtualDevice value into a shell command string. Attackers can reopen the request pipe through /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> and supply a crafted VirtualDevice value such as /dev/null; <command> to achieve arbitrary command execution as root.

The manipulation results in os command injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 26.10.31 is able to address this issue. The patch is identified as 07c73e1434c4c8e49094396c7d93bb09d6f159a4. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component.
